case-sara.text: [Softly] After dinner I notice the apartment is quiet, and I start checking my phone again.
case-sara.suggestion: The quiet settles around you after dinner, and the phone becomes the one small place where he might still appear.

case-sara.text: [Numb] I tell people I'm fine, but I feel flat when I say it.
case-sara.suggestion: Fine comes out smooth, while something underneath has gone pale and still.

case-sara.text: [Sad] I found his jacket in the closet and stood there longer than made sense.
case-sara.suggestion: That jacket stops you in the doorway, a small piece of him pulling the whole loss back into the room.

case-sara.text: [Softly] Some mornings I forget for a second, and then I remember we are not together.
case-sara.suggestion: There is that one clear second, then the breakup drops back onto you like weight returning to the bed.

case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] When friends ask how I am, I give a short answer and change the subject.
case-sara.suggestion: The short answer closes the door quickly, while the real answer waits tight in your throat.

case-sara.text: [Sad] I stay on my phone late because going to sleep feels hard now.
case-sara.suggestion: It is as if the little light of the phone keeps you company when the night feels hard to face.

case-sara.text: [Softly] A song came on in a store, and I had to leave before I cried.
case-sara.suggestion: The first notes find you in the aisle, and suddenly grief is right there under the fluorescent lights.

case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] I keep thinking maybe I did something wrong, but I can't pin down what.
case-sara.suggestion: The mind keeps searching for the flaw, like if it can find the loose thread, the whole leaving might make sense.

case-sara.text: [Sad] Some nights I sit on the floor beside the bed for a while instead of getting in.
case-sara.suggestion: The floor becomes the place you fold into when the bed feels too exposed and wide.

case-sara.text: [Softly] When you are kind to me, I feel awkward and look away.
case-sara.suggestion: Kindness comes close, and it is almost too warm to take in, so your eyes drop to safer ground.

case-sara.text: [Matter-of-fact] I took his name off the mailbox. It needed doing. Coming home afterwards was harder than I expected.
case-sara.suggestion: As if that small change at the door made the absence inside feel much larger.

case-sara.text: [Controlled] I keep the evenings busy. When there's nothing planned, I notice how much I miss having someone to tell the little things to.
case-sara.suggestion: All the activity goes quiet, and there's that empty place where the day's little stories used to go.

case-michael.text: [Firm] When someone corrects me in front of the team, I get hot and stop listening.
case-michael.suggestion: It sounds like the heat rises as though a spotlight has suddenly swung onto you in front of everyone.

case-michael.text: [Tense] I go into meetings expecting people to mess up, and I hate that I do that.
case-michael.suggestion: You arrive already braced, like part of you is standing guard at the door before anyone speaks.

case-michael.text: [Tense] By the end of the day I realize how many comments I did not say.
case-michael.suggestion: It is as if the whole day is clenched shut, every sharp sentence still held behind your teeth.

case-michael.text: [Embarrassed] After I snap, I feel embarrassed, but I mostly try not to think about it.
case-michael.suggestion: The embarrassment sits there afterward, heavy and damp, while you try to step around it.

case-michael.text: [Defensive] When my wife sighs while I am explaining something, I assume she has already decided I am wrong.
case-michael.suggestion: That small sigh can cross the room like a charge, and your system braces before she has even spoken.

case-michael.text: [Tense] If someone says calm down during an argument, I get angrier immediately and stop hearing the rest.
case-michael.suggestion: It is as if those two words strike a match, and the anger flares before you can hear anything else.

case-michael.text: [Embarrassed] When I don't know the answer in a meeting, I feel exposed in front of everyone.
case-michael.suggestion: Not knowing opens a bare place, like all the competence you rely on has lost its cover for a second.

case-michael.text: [Defensive] I slam doors sometimes because I don't know what else to do with the feeling.
case-michael.suggestion: The door takes the feeling for you, loud enough to cover the smaller sting underneath.

case-michael.text: [Ashamed] After a fight, thinking about apologizing first makes me feel weak and smaller than her.
case-michael.suggestion: The apology feels like stepping onto lower ground, with everyone suddenly taller around you.

case-michael.text: [Ashamed] At night I replay the argument and hear how sharp I sounded.
case-michael.suggestion: The house goes quiet, but your own voice keeps echoing in the kitchen, still cutting after the fight is over.

case-michael.text: [Clipped] One small correction in a good report. I heard nothing else they said. That's irritating.
case-michael.suggestion: That one correction takes up the whole room, and the good work shrinks out of sight.

case-michael.text: [Controlled] I know my son is just asking for help. Still, when I can't answer straight away, I feel as if I've failed him.
case-michael.suggestion: Even a small question seems to put you under a spotlight where you have to know the answer immediately.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] When it's my turn in a meeting, I lose track of what I was going to say.
case-jason.suggestion: It is as if every face turns toward you and the sentence you had ready vanishes into thin air.

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] In meetings I keep my hands under the table because I worry people will notice me.
case-jason.suggestion: Even your hands have to stay hidden, as if one small sign could give you away.

case-jason.text: [Anxious] I practice what to say, but when people look at me, I freeze.
case-jason.suggestion: All the practiced words line up, then the eyes land on you and everything locks behind a sheet of ice.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] If people laugh nearby after I have spoken, I assume I did something strange.
case-jason.suggestion: The laugh travels across the room and points itself at you, even before you know what it was about.

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] When attention turns to me, I get quieter and try not to move much.
case-jason.suggestion: Your whole body starts shrinking in the chair, trying to stay present without being seen.

case-jason.text: [Anxious] When someone compliments me after a meeting, I smile, but I don't really believe it.
case-jason.suggestion: It is as if the compliment stops at the door. You hear it, but it does not quite get in.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] Sunday night I start feeling low when the apartment gets quiet, but I mostly just scroll.
case-jason.suggestion: The week arrives early in the room, and scrolling becomes a small moving light against the heaviness.

case-jason.text: [Quiet and ashamed] I rewrite simple messages over and over, then sometimes don't send them.
case-jason.suggestion: One small message becomes a narrow doorway, and every rewrite is another step back from being seen.

case-jason.text: [Anxious] Even saying hello in the hallway can sound wrong to me afterward.
case-jason.suggestion: That tiny hello keeps ringing in your ears, as if one ordinary word has become evidence against you.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] In groups, I keep track of where the exit is before I join the conversation.
case-jason.suggestion: The exit becomes the safest part of the room, the place your eyes hold onto when attention feels too close.

case-jason.text: [Flat] Everyone in the group chat seemed to know what to say. I wrote a reply, looked at it, and didn't send it.
case-jason.suggestion: The conversation keeps moving, and you're waiting at its edge with words you can't quite let out.

case-jason.text: [Matter-of-fact] I replayed the greeting all evening. It lasted about five seconds. It's annoying that I can't leave it alone.
case-jason.suggestion: Those five seconds keep circling back, like a tiny clip you can't stop playing.

case-arne.text: [Flatly] I make coffee. One cup now. That’s how mornings go.
case-arne.suggestion: Almost as though the morning still sets a place for two, and you meet the empty one. Does that capture it?

case-arne.text: [Distant] There’s nobody to show the repaired gate to. Just a gate that works.
case-arne.suggestion: The job is finished, but the little moment of calling her over has nowhere to go. Is it like that?

case-arne.text: [Matter-of-fact] Her side of the wardrobe is still full. Mine hasn’t changed either.
case-arne.suggestion: Two sides still waiting there, though only one person gets dressed. What is that like for you?

case-arne.text: [Flatly] After Emma leaves, I turn the radio up. It fills the time.
case-arne.suggestion: Maybe the radio puts a voice into the space her leaving opens. Does that fit, or not quite?

case-arne.text: [Distant] Her recipe is in the drawer. Grease mark and all.
case-arne.suggestion: That mark is almost a little trace of her standing there, cooking. What happens as you picture it?

case-arne.text: [Flatly] The bed is easier to make. Half of it isn’t used.
case-arne.suggestion: That neat, untouched half can say she’s missing without any words. Is that close to your experience?

case-arne.text: [Matter-of-fact] I listen for her when a floorboard creaks. Then I remember.
case-arne.suggestion: For a second, the familiar sound almost brings her into the next room. Then the quiet returns. Does that fit?

case-arne.text: [Distant] I keep the photograph where I can see it from the chair.
case-arne.suggestion: A familiar face keeping a place in the room with you. Is that what having it there offers?

case-arne.text: [Flatly] At the workshop I forgot to check the time. I used to check it constantly.
case-arne.suggestion: For that afternoon, the clock loosened its grip. What is it like to put it that way?

case-arne.text: [Matter-of-fact] I have small things to tell her. Weather. Tom’s joke.
case-arne.suggestion: Those little pieces of your day still turn toward her. Does that sound right?

case-arne.text: [Distant] Sundays are long. I look at the time until dinner.
case-arne.suggestion: Almost as though Sunday has lost its familiar gathering point. Is that the long feeling?

case-arne.text: [Flatly] Her handwriting is still on the label. Mine is underneath.
case-arne.suggestion: Your two handwritings still side by side. Could we pause with what you notice seeing them?

case-arne.text: [Distant] A quiet breakfast. Nice, objectively. Then the guilt starts.
case-arne.suggestion: Almost as though a small bit of peace is allowed in, then stopped at the door. Does that capture anything?

case-arne.text: [Flatly] I’m off duty now. Strange phrase for your wife, but there it is.
case-arne.suggestion: The watch has ended, while being her husband hasn’t simply ended inside you. Is that close?

case-arne.text: [Matter-of-fact] The workshop is noisy. Home isn’t. That’s the difference.
case-arne.suggestion: Coming from voices and tools into a room where nobody answers—what is that contrast like?

case-arne.text: [Distant] I keep her coat, but move my own things around it.
case-arne.suggestion: You’re making room to live around something of her you want nearby. Does that image fit?

case-arne.text: [Flatly] I tell the good story about her. People like that one.
case-arne.suggestion: Almost a polished story you can hand over, while other parts stay with you. Is that how it feels?

case-arne.text: [Dryly] Emma visits. I put my capable face on. We have tea.
case-arne.suggestion: As if the visit has a place for the capable Leo, but not much space for the lonely one. Does that fit?

case-arne.text: [Distant] The laugh was there, the guilt was there. A busy afternoon.
case-arne.suggestion: Enjoyment with a shadow arriving beside it. Is “shadow” close, or does another image fit better?

case-arne.text: [Flatly] I sleep now. The house doesn’t need me awake.
case-arne.suggestion: A quiet house, with no call to get up for. What is it like to picture that change?

case-arne.text: [Matter-of-fact] There’s a list of unfinished jobs. Nothing urgent. I read it anyway.
case-arne.suggestion: Almost something to hold onto when the day has lost its familiar shape. Does that come close?

case-arne.text: [Distant] I can remember her laughing or remember the illness. Different files.
case-arne.suggestion: Two parts of your life with her kept apart, perhaps because bringing them together feels difficult. Is it like that?

case-arne.text: [Flatly] Tom’s offer is there. I don’t use it.
case-arne.suggestion: A door left open, with you still outside it. Does that image fit, or is it different?

case-arne.text: [Distant] Sundays are either full of visitors or entirely empty.
case-arne.suggestion: As if there’s no comfortable middle space yet. Does that describe what you’re missing?

case-arne.text: [Distant, firm] The chair is empty. Don’t make it a symbol of my whole life.
case-arne.suggestion: We can keep it to this chair, this evening. What is it like to picture the room at that small scale?

case-arne.text: [Flatly] Home after the workshop feels like changing languages. Don’t know what I mean.
case-arne.suggestion: Perhaps the afternoon has voices that don’t carry into the house. Is that close, or would you keep your own image?

case-arne.text: [Watchful] No “waves of grief,” please. It’s more ordinary than that.
case-arne.suggestion: Then let’s keep it ordinary: making coffee and finding only your cup there. Does that moment fit today?

case-arne.text: [Distant] I tell a cheerful story and feel myself leave the room a little.
case-arne.suggestion: Almost as if the story is present while part of you stands back. Does that fit, or is “leave” different?

case-arne.text: [Dryly] I’m off duty. Don’t call it freedom; that’s too grand.
case-arne.suggestion: Off duty may be the right size: no next task waiting, and an unfamiliar pause. What is that pause like?

case-arne.text: [Flatly] Her recipe looks like a conversation I can’t finish.
case-arne.suggestion: A line from her still on the page, with your reply having nowhere to reach her. Is that close to your image?

case-arne.text: [Distant] The good day doesn’t fit. Like a key to the old lock.
case-arne.suggestion: There’s enjoyment, and the familiar way of letting it belong doesn’t work as before. Does that follow your key image?

case-arne.text: [Watchful] I can picture her laughing. I won’t recreate her last days for you.
case-arne.suggestion: We can stay with the laugh only. Is there one ordinary detail of it you want to bring close?

case-arne.text: [Flatly] I can put the coat away. It’s the hallway afterward I can’t picture.
case-arne.suggestion: Perhaps the changed hallway feels like stepping into something not yet familiar. Does that capture anything?

case-arne.text: [Distant, half-smile] My hands know the workbench. The rest of me is less certain.
case-arne.suggestion: Your hands finding a familiar task while the rest catches up—does that image fit your afternoon?

case-arne.text: [Dryly] Visitors fill the room. They don’t always fill the lonely part.
case-arne.suggestion: People all around, with a space in the conversation where you’re still missing company. Is that near it?

case-arne.text: [Quiet, distant] I don’t want an image. The plain words are “I miss her.”
case-arne.suggestion: Then we’ll stay with your plain words. We can let them have a moment without adding a picture.

case-mia.text: [Distant] The drawing is unfinished. That’s the situation.
case-mia.suggestion: Is it like the pencil stops while the picture you want to make is still going?

case-mia.text: [Flatly] They talk about me as though I’m not in the meeting.
case-mia.suggestion: Is it like being in the room but left outside the conversation?

case-mia.text: [Matter-of-fact] I have to explain the fatigue again every time.
case-mia.suggestion: Does it feel like starting from the beginning each time you need to be believed?

case-mia.text: [Distant] My good day is the one they remember.
case-mia.suggestion: Is that one day becoming the whole picture they have of you?

case-mia.text: [Quietly] The sketchbook is there, but I leave it shut.
case-mia.suggestion: When you picture it closed beside you, does it bring the missing part closer?

case-mia.text: [Flatly] Alex’s help gets ahead of me.
case-mia.suggestion: Is it like he reaches the answer while you’re still deciding what you want?

case-mia.text: [Distant] I used to give the whole tour. Now I give part of it.
case-mia.suggestion: Does handing over the rest of the tour make the loss of that familiar role more vivid?

case-mia.text: [Matter-of-fact] Sam left the chair where I needed it.
case-mia.suggestion: Is it a small sign that your place in the room has been thought about?

case-mia.text: [Distant] I cancel the visit, and the afternoon is empty.
case-mia.suggestion: When you picture that empty afternoon, is it the missing company that stands out?

case-mia.text: [Quietly] I’m tired of describing myself as a list of limits.
case-mia.suggestion: Is it like the things you love get left out of the introduction?

case-mia.text: [Flatly] I looked at the plants while Ella did the watering.
case-mia.suggestion: Did watching bring the wish to be the one doing it closer, or was it something else?

case-mia.text: [Distant] When I spoke about the painting, they stopped and listened.
case-mia.suggestion: Is it like your voice had a place again, in that moment?

case-mia.text: [Distant] Alex does the helpful thing. I’m somewhere behind it, getting cross.
case-mia.suggestion: Is it like the task moves forward while your chance to choose gets left behind?

case-mia.text: [Flatly] I carry a whole explanation around for the next person who asks.
case-mia.suggestion: Is it like having to bring the evidence with you before your need can have a place?

case-mia.text: [Practical] Three days leaves more room, but less of my old working life.
case-mia.suggestion: Is that extra space also showing you the part of work you miss?

case-mia.text: [Distant] I say “fine” and the conversation closes. Convenient, I suppose.
case-mia.suggestion: Does “fine” act like closing a door before anyone sees the difficult part?

case-mia.text: [Quietly] I kept the pencil beside me, even after I stopped.
case-mia.suggestion: Was keeping it there a way of not quite saying goodbye to that evening’s drawing?

case-mia.text: [Matter-of-fact] They see the good day. I’m the one who has the day after it.
case-mia.suggestion: Is it like they see one page while you’re living the pages that follow too?

case-mia.text: [Distant] There’s help everywhere and not much room for me in it.
case-mia.suggestion: Is it like the room fills with solutions before your own voice has somewhere to sit?

case-mia.text: [Flatly] I chose the music. That was my little job.
case-mia.suggestion: When you picture choosing it, does that “little job” hold a real place for you?

case-mia.text: [Distant] I’m proud of the tour. Also watching the clock the whole time.
case-mia.suggestion: Does the clock sit beside the pride, reminding you that your energy has an end?

case-mia.text: [Quietly] I want to be helped, not handled. Those are my words.
case-mia.suggestion: “Handled” sounds like decisions happening around you rather than with you. Does that bring it closer?

case-mia.text: [Flatly] Ella’s visit becomes a list of things she can do.
case-mia.suggestion: Is the list leaving out the part where you just get to be sisters?

case-mia.text: [Distant] Sam waited for my answer. It felt like an unusual amount of time.
case-mia.suggestion: Was that pause a space where your answer could arrive, instead of being supplied for you?

case-mia.text: [Distant] I’m consulted after the practical arrangements are settled. That’s apparently choice.
case-mia.suggestion: Is it like being handed a place in a picture that was drawn before you arrived?

case-mia.text: [Flatly] My explanation is polished. Nobody hears the part I haven’t polished.
case-mia.suggestion: Is there a more uneven, unfinished part just outside that explanation? Does that image fit?

case-mia.text: [Corrects, distant] Not trapped. I can leave the meeting. I lose something if I do.
case-mia.suggestion: Is it more like standing at a doorway where either choice has a cost?

case-mia.text: [Quietly] The pencil is there. I don’t want it turned into a symbol of my whole life.
case-mia.suggestion: We can keep it just that pencil. When you picture it, is there a small feeling nearby, or not?

case-mia.text: [Distant] Everyone relaxed on my good day. I had to keep watching the time.
case-mia.suggestion: Is it like they could put the clock away while yours still had to stay in view?

case-mia.text: [Matter-of-fact] I want help at my side, not moving out ahead of me.
case-mia.suggestion: “At my side” sounds like someone matching your pace rather than choosing the route. Is that close?

case-mia.text: [Flatly] The shorter tour has space for my body. Less space for the bits I loved.
case-mia.suggestion: Does that version hold you physically, while leaving some loved parts of the work outside it?

case-mia.text: [Distant] When Ella visits, our old conversations get crowded out by things to do.
case-mia.suggestion: Is it like there’s less room at the table for just the two of you?

case-mia.text: [Quietly] I’m the same person. People seem to arrive with a different script now.
case-mia.suggestion: Is it as if you recognize yourself, but not the part they’ve written for you?

case-mia.text: [Corrects] Not a wall. I do want company. Your wall image makes me sound closed.
case-mia.suggestion: Would an open door with a wish to be asked before someone enters fit better, or neither image?

case-mia.text: [Distant] I had an ordinary conversation about art. That’s why I remember it.
case-mia.suggestion: Was there a moment where you could be in the conversation without the illness introducing you?

case-mia.text: [Flatly] My own answer takes time. Someone usually puts an answer in that space.
case-mia.suggestion: Is it like the pause gets filled before your words have a chance to arrive?

case-nora.text: [Distant] They wanted the design, just not me presenting it.
case-nora.suggestion: Is it like your work could enter the room while you were kept at the door?

case-nora.text: [Flatly] My answer is Norway. Then comes another question.
case-nora.suggestion: Does it feel like your answer is handed back, marked not enough?

case-nora.text: [Distant] Max’s words take up the space before mine arrive.
case-nora.suggestion: Is it like the pause for your answer gets filled before you can use it?

case-nora.text: [Matter-of-fact] I’ve prepared an explanation for every version of the question.
case-nora.suggestion: Is it like carrying a folder of answers into an ordinary conversation?

case-nora.text: [Quietly] I looked at the drawings, but didn’t want to touch them.
case-nora.suggestion: When you picture them on the desk, does the distance from work you love come closer?

case-nora.text: [Distant] I’m introduced by where my parents came from before what I do.
case-nora.suggestion: Is it like the first page of your introduction is being written for you?

case-nora.text: [Flatly] I held the meeting together and took the feeling home.
case-nora.suggestion: Did you have to carry it out with you because there was no room for it there?

case-nora.text: [Distant] Lina listened. I didn’t have to arrange the story neatly.
case-nora.suggestion: Was there room to put down the messy version with her?

case-nora.text: [Quietly] I’m tired of being asked to prove I belong.
case-nora.suggestion: Is it like having to show a ticket again for a place that is already yours?

case-nora.text: [Flatly] An ordinary conversation about dinner was surprisingly welcome.
case-nora.suggestion: Did it give you a moment where you could just be in the conversation?

case-nora.text: [Distant] I want my own voice in the room.
case-nora.suggestion: When you picture speaking about the design, is that the place you want back?

case-nora.text: [Quietly] The comment stayed after everyone left.
case-nora.suggestion: Was it as if the room emptied but those words were still there with you?

case-nora.text: [Distant] I have a portfolio and an explanation of belonging. Both come to the meeting.
case-nora.suggestion: Is it like carrying two sets of papers when you only wanted to discuss the design?

case-nora.text: [Flatly] They applaud how I cope. The work gets less attention.
case-nora.suggestion: Is the applause standing in front of the work you wanted them to see?

case-nora.text: [Distant] “Norway” opens the next question instead of closing the first.
case-nora.suggestion: Does it feel like the doorway moves each time you reach it?

case-nora.text: [Matter-of-fact] I kept the conversation smooth. The rough part waited at home.
case-nora.suggestion: Was there a rough, unfinished version you had to carry away by yourself?

case-nora.text: [Quietly] Max’s help can crowd me out. That’s my phrase.
case-nora.suggestion: “Crowd me out” sounds like less space for you inside the very support you want. Is that close?

case-nora.text: [Distant] I’m always preparing the next explanation.
case-nora.suggestion: Is it like sitting in today’s conversation with tomorrow’s defense already beside you?

case-nora.text: [Flatly] Lina heard the story without making me line everything up.
case-nora.suggestion: Did it give you somewhere to put the pieces down without arranging them first?

case-nora.text: [Distant] I’ve become the person they ask about diversity before architecture.
case-nora.suggestion: Is one part of your introduction being enlarged until the architect is hard to see?

case-nora.text: [Quietly] I can stay, at a cost. I can leave, at a cost.
case-nora.suggestion: Is it like standing at a junction where neither road leaves everything behind?

case-nora.text: [Distant] An ordinary evening felt like a place I’d forgotten I could have.
case-nora.suggestion: When you picture dinner with your friends, does that ordinary place come closer?

case-nora.text: [Flatly] I want the credit without a spotlight on how generous they are.
case-nora.suggestion: Is it like wanting the light on your work rather than on the people handing it back?

case-nora.text: [Distant] I have a voice, and an acceptable version of that voice for meetings.
case-nora.suggestion: Is the meeting version leaving out some words you still need heard?

case-nora.text: [Distant] My work is on the table. My place at the table becomes the discussion.
case-nora.suggestion: Is it like the drawings wait while you have to justify the chair you’re sitting in?

case-nora.text: [Flatly] I’ve polished the explanation. The part I haven’t polished is mine alone.
case-nora.suggestion: Is there an unfinished version sitting just outside the account everyone hears? Does that fit?

case-nora.text: [Corrects, distant] Not between cultures. Between wanting my job and not wanting this treatment.
case-nora.suggestion: Is it more like two important wishes that won’t fit easily in the same room?

case-nora.text: [Quietly] The drawings are just drawings today. Don’t load them with everything.
case-nora.suggestion: We can keep them just drawings. When you picture the desk, is any small feeling there, or not?

case-nora.text: [Distant] A simple request becomes a whole presentation about why I’m reasonable.
case-nora.suggestion: Is it like wrapping the request in papers before it’s allowed to stand by itself?

case-nora.text: [Matter-of-fact] I want Max beside me. He keeps reaching the answer first.
case-nora.suggestion: “Beside me” sounds like matching your pace rather than arriving ahead of your words. Is that close?

case-nora.text: [Flatly] They recognize the problem. I’m still the person doing the follow-up.
case-nora.suggestion: Does the acknowledgment leave the weight of carrying it forward in your hands?

case-nora.text: [Distant] I chose silence. It wasn’t an empty silence.
case-nora.suggestion: Did that quiet hold choices and costs the room couldn’t see?

case-nora.text: [Quietly] I’m tired of the acceptable version of this story.
case-nora.suggestion: Is there a less tidy version waiting for somewhere it doesn’t have to be acceptable?

case-nora.text: [Corrects] Not a wall. I want company. I don’t want people walking straight into the story.
case-nora.suggestion: Would an open door with a request to knock fit better, or neither image?

case-nora.text: [Distant] We talked about photographs. I didn’t have to introduce the problem first.
case-nora.suggestion: Was there space to enter as the person enjoying the pictures, with no explanation at the door?

case-nora.text: [Flatly] Leaving wouldn’t give back the part of this job I liked.
case-nora.suggestion: When you picture leaving, is the loved part still there behind you, rather than simply gone?
